ROUND 2 of 2, final C34 performance verdict: PASS-WITH-NOTES.
Subject: pr:318
Head: 47d828a9c33b855b7ad58eb7da9ecdc84fdac0a0

The re-priced per-pane and per-drain costs are accurate. The capture-rate table now correctly limits 2D+R to settled short drains and includes per-tick captures during a longer in-flight drain. No new timer, poll, SQL, event publication or process-launch site was added by R318-001. No demonstrated normal-use resource-cost regression blocks this final head. One newly checked injection-multiplier nuance is a C34 follow-up only.

Verified final-round costs:
- Observer: one extra shared synchronous gate-mutex acquisition per pane reaching the drain path; copy TapDrains {started,ended} (two u64s) and compute settled(). Replay uses the EXISTING observed() snapshot and adds no second gate lock. At the packet's217 panes/600ms, nominal361.67 added acquisitions/s. Backoff/refused panes skip this path; shared-lock waiting is possible.
- Drain: two lock/entry sections, one before the drain and one in DrainEnd::drop. Each allocates a pane.to_string key even for an occupied entry. The drop guard itself holds borrowed gate/pane references, with no separate heap allocation or async task. Neither critical section holds the mutex across the drain await. Counts update on success/error/cancellation once the guard exists.
- State: two scalar counters per gate pane; the observer keeps an optional settled count per LastCapture. Metadata remains O(panes), not a history per drain. Per-tick lookup copies counters, not the composer string; the existing replay snapshot/string work remains.
- Captures: a settled overlap can cause two captures, so 2D+R is the right SHORT-DRAIN model, with coalescing and already-active panes reducing added work. A drain spanning several ticks yields settled()==None and can force one observer capture per pane/pass until it ends, then a fresh settled baseline. It is not a global 2D+R bound independent of drain duration. The PR now explicitly states this. The gross nominal observer envelope remains one capture/pane/pass,217/0.6=361.67/s, and the30s backstop is unchanged.
- Transport: the round2 dead-reader change is documentation, not a reader-liveness poll. Normal captures use the existing persistent tmux control client; its inherited Fork fallback and repair/reader startup retain their counted old launch costs. No NEW process-launch site is a valid claim, not an absolute no-launch guarantee on every inherited path.
